h1: The 6 Best NAS Storage Devices for Home Office of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Home Office NAS 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six two-bay NAS devices for home offices, compared on processor, caching, network speed and software.
summary: The Synology DS225+ is our best home office NAS thanks to its Intel CPU with hardware transcoding and mature DSM software. The Asustor AS5402T adds NVMe caching and dual 2.5GbE, and the UGREEN DXP2800 is the non-Synology alternative. The UGREEN DH2300 is the cheap entry and the BUFFALO ships with drives included.
intro: The first NAS mistake is buying the enclosure and forgetting the drives. Most of the boxes below are diskless, so the real cost is the enclosure plus two hard drives, and the cheapest enclosure rarely makes the cheapest finished system. The second mistake is paying for transcoding power when the job is just backing up documents.

We reviewed six two-bay NAS devices on paper, comparing processor, memory, network ports, caching, software and whether drives come in the box. All are priced between $100 and $500 for the enclosure, and drives are an extra cost on every diskless unit.

products.name: Synology DS225+
products.verdict: Real transcoding power and the most polished NAS software.
products.description:
The DS225+ is a two-bay diskless NAS with an Intel CPU and hardware transcoding. It runs Synology DSM, which includes Synology Drive, Synology Photos and Surveillance Station.

It ranks first because the Intel CPU with transcoding sets it apart from the ARM and entry models below it, and DSM is the best-known NAS software. The tradeoff is cost, since the enclosure sits in the $200 to $500 bucket and drives are sold separately.

Buy it for a home office that runs backups, photos and media streaming from one box. Skip it if you only need basic file storage.
products.idealFor: Offices needing backups plus media and photos.
products.skipIf: You only need basic file storage.

products.name: Asustor AS5402T
products.verdict: Four NVMe cache slots and dual 2.5GbE ports.
products.description:
Inside the AS5402T you get a 2.0GHz quad-core Intel processor with 4GB of DDR4 memory, plus four M.2 NVMe SSD slots and a pair of 2.5GbE ports. Those NVMe slots let you build a cache that speeds up files you open often.

It ranks second because the hardware beats the Synology on raw network and caching options, while the software is less familiar to many buyers. It also sits in the $200 to $500 bucket.

Buy it if your team moves large files and wants faster-than-gigabit links. Skip it if you want the simplest software.
products.idealFor: Creators and teams moving large files.

products.name: UGREEN NAS DXP2800
products.verdict: A two-bay box aimed at creators who want something different.
products.description:
The DXP2800 is a two-bay diskless NAS running UGREEN NASync OS, positioned for content creators and enthusiasts.

It ranks third because the listing offers fewer hardware specifics than the Synology and Asustor above. UGREEN's pitch is a competitive price and a fresh software stack. Pricing falls in the $200 to $500 range.

Buy it if you want to try a newer platform. Skip it if you want a long track record.
products.idealFor: Creators open to a newer platform.

products.name: Synology DS223
products.verdict: Synology's software without the transcoding premium.
products.description:
The DS223 is a two-bay diskless NAS running the DSM software ecosystem, positioned as a home and office backup hub.

It ranks fourth because it lacks the transcoding hardware of the DS225+, so media streaming is weaker. It is a sensible choice for pure backup and file sharing. Pricing sits in the $200 to $500 bucket.

Buy it if you want Synology's software for documents and backups. Skip it if you will stream or transcode video.

products.name: BUFFALO LinkStation 720 4TB
products.verdict: Ships with 4TB of drives, so there is no extra shopping.
products.description:
The LinkStation 720 is a two-bay NAS that ships with 4TB of drives installed. It is positioned for private cloud storage in a home office.

It ranks fifth because the listing gives little hardware detail beyond the drives, but it is the only pick with drives pre-installed. That makes its price easier to compare. It lands in the $200 to $500 bucket.

Buy it if you want one purchase and no drive shopping. Skip it if you need transcoding or fast networking.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want an all-in-one price.
products.skipIf: You want to choose your own drives.

products.name: UGREEN NAS DH2300
products.verdict: The cheapest enclosure here, with 64TB of capacity support.
products.description:
Pitched as a desktop box with two bays, the DH2300 can address as much as 64TB across both drives. It has the lowest enclosure cost in this guide, in the $100 to $200 bucket, and arrives with no drives.

It ranks last because the listing lists few performance specs, so it fits light duties best. The price is the draw.

Buy it as a first NAS for backups and sharing. Skip it if you need transcoding or caching.

methodology.title: Caching
methodology.description: NVMe cache slots earned credit for speeding up frequent files.

methodology.title: Software
methodology.description: We compared the maturity of each platform's file, photo and backup apps.

methodology.title: Total cost
methodology.description: We considered whether drives are included, since they add to the real price.

whatMatters.detail: Most NAS enclosures are diskless, so you must buy drives. This matters because two drives can cost as much as the box. Check the title for 'diskless' or an included capacity such as 4TB.
Transcoding converts video on the fly for different devices. Intel CPUs with hardware transcoding handle it smoothly. Look for 'hardware transcoding' in the listing.
2.5GbE ports move files faster than gigabit if your router and computer support them. Otherwise they are unused. Check the port count and speed.
A cache keeps frequently used files on fast SSD storage. It helps with large project folders. Look for M.2 NVMe slots in the specs.
NAS software handles backups, photos and file sharing. A mature platform saves setup time. Check which apps are named in the listing.

howToChoose.intro: Start from what the NAS will do every day.

cards.label: Diskless
cards.text: Lets you pick drive brand and size but needs extra purchase. Picks: DS225+, DS223, DXP2800, AS5402T, DH2300.

cards.label: Drives included
cards.text: Ships ready to run with 4TB installed. Pick: BUFFALO LinkStation 720.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers should choose diskless for flexibility unless they want the simplest purchase.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Reliable file sharing, scheduled backups and enough speed for several users.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Synology DS225+ offers the best software and transcoding, while the Asustor AS5402T has the best network links.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You stream video or move big files. The DS225+ and AS5402T pay off.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only need backups. The DS223 or DH2300 is enough.

faq.q: Do I need to buy drives separately?
faq.a: For most of these units, yes. Only the BUFFALO LinkStation 720 ships with drives installed.
Use drives rated for NAS use, which are built for continuous operation. Check the maker's compatibility list before buying.

faq.q: Is the DS225+ worth it over the DS223?
faq.a: If you stream or transcode video, yes. For backups alone the DS223 is enough.

faq.q: How do I set up a two-bay NAS?
faq.a: Install drives, connect to your router and follow the setup wizard. Then create storage and shared folders.
No. A mirrored pair protects against one drive failing but not deletion or ransomware. Keep a second backup.
Only if your router and computers also support it. Otherwise the speed benefit is unused.

finalTake: The Synology DS225+ is the best NAS for most home offices, with transcoding hardware and the strongest software. The Asustor AS5402T is the pick for speed, and the DS223 handles plain backups. Choose the BUFFALO for a drives-included purchase and the DH2300 for the lowest entry cost.
